THE call for a mod printing its own line into the local chat on 26.2. Does not touch the chat log and is not gated on the player's chat settings. Compile-verified end to end: Minecraft.getInstance().gui.hud.getChat().addClientSystemMessage(Component.literal(msg)).

Second param is `remote`, NOT `overlay`. Decompiled: remote=true -> addServerSystemMessage + logSystemMessage; remote=false -> addClientSystemMessage. Whole method is wrapped in `receiver.chatAbilities().canReceiveSystemMessages()`, so it can silently drop your message. Separate `public void handleOverlay(net.minecraft.network.chat.Component);` handles the action bar.

Compiles and works, but decompiled body is `this.minecraft.gui.chatListener().handleSystemMessage(message, true)` — remote=TRUE, so your mod's own line is recorded as a server message in the chat log and is suppressed if canReceiveSystemMessages() is false. Prefer gui.hud.getChat().addClientSystemMessage(...) for mod output. Note the base net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player.sendSystemMessage(Component) has an EMPTY body — calling it on a Player-typed reference silently does nothing.

Reached via LocalPlayer.chatAbilities(). This is the gate that can swallow a handleSystemMessage / sendSystemMessage call.

DOES NOT EXIST on 26.2. Compile probe: `error: cannot find symbol / symbol: class ResourceLocation / location: package net.minecraft.resources`. Renamed to net.minecraft.resources.Identifier (present in minecraft-common.jar, and it is what Holder.is(...) and ChatComponent's id constants take).

gotchas: ItemStack.is(...) has SIX overloads on 26.2, five of them inherited defaults you will not see in a javap dump of ItemStack. javac's candidate list for a bad call is authoritative: TypedInstance.is(TagKey<Item>), is(HolderSet<Item>), is(Item), is(Holder<Item>), is(ResourceKey<Item>), and ItemStack.is(Predicate<Holder<Item>>). ItemStack implements ItemInstance -> TypedInstance<Item>, which is where the first five come from.

Simplest verified way to test 'this stack is Items.GLOWSTONE' is `stack.is(Items.GLOWSTONE)` — compile-verified. `stack.getItem() == Items.GLOWSTONE` is equally valid (getItem() is literally typeHolder().value()). The lambda form `stack.is(h -> h.value() == Items.GLOWSTONE)` also compiles but buys nothing.

The project note is HALF WRONG. isIn(TagKey) is indeed gone, but `stack.is(ItemTags.SWORDS)` compiles directly via TypedInstance.is(TagKey<T>) — compile-verified. The `stack.is(h -> h.is(ItemTags.SWORDS))` workaround is unnecessary; keep the lambda form only when you need to combine several holder predicates in one pass.

TypedInstance.is(Holder<T>) compares Holder REFERENCES (`this.typeHolder() == type`), not values. Passing a Holder you constructed yourself will always be false. is(T) and is(ResourceKey<T>) compare by value/key and are safe.

Direction.getNormal() is gone. Use getUnitVec3i() for the Vec3i, getUnitVec3() for a Vec3, getUnitVec3f() for a JOML Vector3fc, or getStepX/Y/Z() for the ints. Pre-26.2 code calling getNormal() will not compile.

BlockPos.offset(Direction) is gone as an instance method — only offset(int,int,int) and offset(Vec3i) remain, so `pos.offset(dir)` fails with a confusing 'Direction cannot be converted to Vec3i' rather than 'no such method'. Use pos.relative(dir). The static long forms BlockPos.offset(long, Direction) and offset(long,int,int,int) DO take a Direction — easy to misread as proof the instance form still exists.

Gui was split in 26.2. Minecraft.gui is still there, but the HUD moved into a new net.minecraft.client.gui.Hud reachable via the public final field Gui.hud. Gui.getChat() no longer exists; the chain is Minecraft.getInstance().gui.hud.getChat().

ChatComponent.addMessage(Component) no longer exists — the only addMessage is private and takes (Component, MessageSignature, GuiMessageSource, GuiMessageTag). For a mod printing its own line, call addClientSystemMessage(Component). addServerSystemMessage(Component) is for genuine server traffic and additionally writes to the chat log / report context.

LocalPlayer.sendSystemMessage(Component) compiles and works, but it forwards with remote=TRUE (`chatListener().handleSystemMessage(message, true)`), so your mod's output is filed as a server message and gets logged. Worse, handleSystemMessage is entirely wrapped in `receiver.chatAbilities().canReceiveSystemMessages()` — a player with system messages off will never see your line, with no error. addClientSystemMessage bypasses both.

ChatListener.handleSystemMessage(Component, boolean)'s boolean is `remote`, not `overlay` as the older signature's second parameter suggested. Passing true routes to chat-as-if-from-server; passing false routes to addClientSystemMessage. The action bar is a separate method, handleOverlay(Component).

net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player.sendSystemMessage(Component) has an EMPTY body on 26.2 (verified in the decompiled source). If your code holds a Player-typed reference rather than LocalPlayer, the call silently vanishes.
Player.displayClientMessage(Component, boolean) is gone entirely, on both Player and LocalPlayer.

net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation no longer exists; it is net.minecraft.resources.Identifier. This bites indirectly — Holder.is(Identifier) and the Identifier constants on ChatComponent will look like unrelated errors if you still import ResourceLocation.

isEmptyBlock(BlockPos) survives, but it is a default on LevelReader, NOT on BlockGetter. BlockGetter only declares getBlockState/getFluidState/getBlockEntity. If you type a parameter as BlockGetter (a common narrowing for helper methods) isEmptyBlock will not resolve — take LevelReader or ClientLevel.

RespawnAnchorBlock.canSetSpawn(ServerLevel, BlockPos) is SERVER-ONLY and uncallable from client code. Its entire body on 26.2 is `level.environmentAttributes().getValue(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS, pos)`, and Level.environmentAttributes() is available on ClientLevel — so the client can reproduce the check exactly. Do NOT reimplement the old hardcoded 'dimension == NETHER' test; 26.2 made this data-driven per dimension, so a datapack dimension can flip it.

RespawnAnchorBlock.charge(Entity, Level, BlockPos, BlockState) takes plain Level, so it compiles in client code — but it calls level.setBlock / gameEvent / playSound. From a client module it only produces a local desync, never a real charge. Send a genuine interaction packet instead.

Other server-only surface adjacent to this module: ItemStack.hurtAndBreak(int, ServerLevel, ServerPlayer, Consumer<Item>), and BlockStateBase.tick / randomTick / spawnAfterBreak / onExplosionHit / affectNeighborsAfterRemoval all take ServerLevel. There is no client-side equivalent for these; a client module must predict rather than call them.

BlockState declares almost nothing itself. getValue(Property<T>) lives on StateHolder, and getBlock() / isAir() / getFluidState() / the 2-arg is(TagKey, Predicate) live on BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase. `javap -p net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState` is nearly empty and will make you think these methods are gone — dump BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase and StateHolder instead.

When probing 26.2 with javac, put org.jspecify:jspecify and com.mojang:brigadier on the classpath. Without jspecify, javac fails with 'cannot access Nullable' and then reports a TRUNCATED overload set for the affected class — this made LivingEntity.swing(InteractionHand, boolean) look like it did not exist. Both swing overloads are real.
Items.GLOWSTONE and Items.GLOWSTONE_DUST are both present. The anchor is charged with GLOWSTONE (the block item); GLOWSTONE_DUST will fail silently in an item check.
